'''Asai Shrine''' (浅井神社, Asai Jinja) is an ancient shrine located in the western part of Ishizutsumi, {{ill|Takaoka, Toyama|ja|高岡市12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, Toyama Prefecture.
The shrine sits on the left bank of the {{ill|Oyabe River|ja|小矢部川12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, and is said to have been founded to pray for the protection and peace of the river, known for its flooding. The area was also an important transportation hub in ancient times on the Hokurikudō route, suggesting the shrine once enjoyed considerable prosperity.
As the guardian deity of irrigation and agriculture, the shrine was believed to prevent flooding of the Oyabe River. It is also thought to ensure the flourishing of river transport on the Oyabe.
Because the shrine hall was enshrined after building embankments in the area, it is also known as "Kawabata no Miya" (Shrine by the River).
==Worshipped deities (Saijin)==
{{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}|qq=}}
; Main deity
* '''{{ill|Mizuhanome|ja|罔象女神12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (Mitsuhanome no Kami)
==History==
* 717 (Yōrō 1) – Shrine founded
* 759 (Tenpyō-hōji 3) – Listed as "one tan of land belonging to Asai no Kami" in the map of lands donated to {{ill|Tōdai-ji|ja|東大寺12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} in Etchū Province
* 1881 (Meiji 14) – Ranked as a gōsha (district shrine), designated for offering of sacred food and cloth by the state
==Shikinai-sha dispute==
This shrine is considered a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|延喜式内社12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Tonami District|ja|礪波郡12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, Etchū Province. However, some claim that the {{ill|Asai Shrine (Fukuoka-chō, Akamaru)|ja|浅井神社 (高岡市福岡町赤丸)12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, located in neighboring Akamaru Village, holds this title instead, leading to ongoing debate.
Because the two shrines in Ishizutsumi and Akamaru are only about 300 meters apart, there is insufficient evidence to make a definitive judgment.
